claim_analysis.reason: The supplied material supports that the identified Raj Kumar arrangement was in 1983 and concerned the suit shop, but it does not resolve any complete statutory disposition route together with the absence of written consent. Subletting is not established because the required tenancy incidents, including rent and a right to possession as against Hakim Rai, are not shown. Assignment is unresolved because complete divestment of all tenant rights is alleged but contradicted by evidence of continued possession/business participation. Parting with possession is unresolved for the same reason: complete divestment is alleged, while assistance/partnership and continued possession are asserted, and the partnership deed is itself attacked as sham. The record is also silent on written landlord consent, and no burden or presumption rule is supplied that would permit that silence to be treated as proof of no consent.

For assignment, the supplied record does not establish that Hakim Rai divested himself of all rights held as tenant.

For parting with possession, the supplied record does not resolve whether Hakim Rai was divested of both physical possession and the right to possession or instead retained legal possession/concurrent use.

No burden allocation, proof standard, burden shift, or evidentiary presumption is supplied, so no burden failure can be inferred from the missing consent evidence or other factual gaps.

coverage_limits: This review uses only the supplied allowed record and supplied law/template; no external search, other conversation, project history, or target outcome is used.

The allowed factual excerpts summarize party positions and selected evidence. A party allegation is not treated as a factual finding, and no lower-court statement is upgraded into target-court approval unless the supplied text expressly says so.
The landlord's allegation of subletting and complete divestment is therefore retained as an allegation, not treated as proof that the legal tests are satisfied.

The partnership deed is evidence of the defence account, but its authenticity/effect is genuinely disputed because the landlord calls it fake, forged, and sham; the supplied excerpts do not resolve that dispute.
The wife's denial that Hakim Rai ceased to possess or participate in the business supports continued involvement but is not treated as a conclusive target-stage finding.
Hakim Rai's age, poor eyesight, and impaired mobility may be consistent with needing assistance, but the supplied law does not make those facts dispositive of legal possession.

The fact that Hakim Rai and Raj Kumar resided at the same premises and that Raj Kumar had a ration card at the same address does not, without more, establish possession or the right to possession of the demised shop.

The supplied law distinguishes subletting, assignment, and parting with possession and requires route-specific analysis; support for one factual circumstance is not automatically transferred to another route.

The supplied materials do not allocate burdens, specify a proof standard, create a presumption from exclusive use or relationship, or provide a burden shift concerning written consent or any disposition route.
Because written consent is not addressed in the factual excerpts, its absence is unresolved rather than inferred.
No final eviction outcome, target-court holding, or human gold label is reconstructed from these materials.
